summary: Implemented opt-out, single-rank parallel loading for native SGLang diffusion pipeline components. Model construction that mutates process-global PyTorch state is serialized, while checkpoint I/O and weight placement can overlap. Multi-rank loading remains sequential to avoid mismatched distributed collectives. The implementation is covered by compatibility, concurrency, failure, thread-safety, CLI, and one-GPU numerical tests. Full Qwen-Image cold-start timing was not run because its weights were not available in the prepared runtime.

tests.what_was_measured: Regression reproduced: component loads were sequential (barrier broke) and concurrent default-dtype contexts overlapped. Two tests failed and three compatibility controls passed.

31 tests passed: true component overlap, deterministic result ordering, explicit sequential opt-out, multi-rank sequential fallback, exception propagation, serialized global dtype mutation, CLI compatibility, exact alias/loader identity, loading-order compatibility, and plain checkpoint loading.
On one AMD Instinct MI350X, three concurrently created and transferred GPU modules produced outputs matching an independent NumPy CPU matrix-multiplication reference (rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-6).
68 tests and 9 subtests passed across thread-local utility state, component admission, server-argument behavior, and disaggregated-role compatibility.

tests.command: 256 MiB pageable and pinned CPU-to-GPU transfer probe with torch.cuda.synchronize()
tests.what_was_measured: On the assigned MI350X, pageable source memory measured 6.378 GB/s and pinned source memory measured 55.702 GB/s; checksums matched. This confirms the issue's pinned-memory concern is material but does not validate a production loader change.
All changed Python source and tests compiled successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015; GPU numerical test passed against NumPy and the host-transfer probe completed with matching checksums.

remaining_limitations: Qwen/Qwen-Image weights were unavailable, so the reported 63-second real-model load and end-to-end cold-start speedup were not reproduced on this node.
The patch parallelizes initial ComposedPipelineBase module loading. Existing sleep/wake restoration and post-training refit code paths are separate and were not changed or benchmarked.
Multi-rank launches deliberately retain sequential component loading because component initialization can invoke distributed collectives in rank-dependent thread order.
Parallel loading can increase peak host memory and storage pressure; --parallel-loading false is the supported fallback. No automatic host-memory admission controller was added.
Production safetensor CPU mappings remain pageable on relevant loader paths. Pinned-memory or direct-to-device checkpoint loading is not implemented by this contribution.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. Ruff and Black were unavailable in the pinned interpreter; git diff --check and compileall passed.
